parole.significato: A shrub with white flowers, possibly Retama raetam; the juniper of the (King James Version) Old Testament.
parole.testo: Ultimately from a Semitic language. Compare Arabic رَتَم (ratam), Biblical Hebrew רותם

parole.significato: Of or pertaining to the ancient city of Ugarit.
parole.testo: From Ugarit + -ic, via a Semitic medium from Sumerian 𒀀𒃼 (a-gar₃ /⁠agar⁠/, “arable land”).

parole.significato: A garment worn over the torso, with or without sleeves, and of various lengths reaching from the hips to the ankles.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle French tunique, from Latin tunica, possibly from Semitic (compare Aramaic [script needed] (kittuna), Hebrew כותנת (kuttoneth, “coat”), English chiton); or from Etruscan. Existed in Old English as tunece; unknown if that term was lost and then reborrowed later. Doublet of tunica.
